result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): The two answers are close: both put the 7.5x vs. +2.7% gap in concrete numbers, recommend labels and a factual title, and treat 3D and colour as secondary. A wins because it explicitly calls the truncated axis the main problem, and its closing message ('a real win stated plainly') adds useful context (resolved vs. opened, year-over-year) without overstating anything. B explains more clearly why a line chart can use a narrower axis, but its suggested 'consistent, compounding growth' slightly oversells growth of about 0.9% per quarter. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers make the 7.5x vs. +2.7% distortion concrete, give the same fixes, and treat 3D/color as secondary. B labels the axis as the main problem more explicitly and adds useful context (opened vs. resolved, seasonality), but its closing callout wrongly says '+130 tickets/quarter' when +130 is the total change (about 43 per quarter). That is a factual error in the very 'honest' title it recommends. A is accurate throughout and explains why a line chart can use a narrower axis, though its 'compounding growth' phrasing adds a little spin.
